newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs maintain gains, other sectors dull.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs maintain gains, other sectors dull.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCC) held onto their recent gains on Wednesday, but most other sectors were lacklustre, brokers said.
Mideast/east vessels were fixed at a buoyant W60, with westward voyages at W55, after falling as low as W45 last week.
"There's a bit more activity and less tonnage around," one broker said.
Representative of the market was the 260,000 tonne Knock More, fixed at W60 Mideast/China for Unipec.
The West Africa market was stable, VLCCs fixed around W67.5 and 130,000 tonne (Suezmax) vessels at about W95.

An unusual reported fixture was the 123,000 tonne Kalamos on a Nigeria/Pembroke voyage, done at about W95 for Texaco. Most Nigerian crude goes to the U.S., the Mediterranean or Asia rather than northern Europe.
The Mediterranean and inter-U.K./Cont markets were quiet. Med Suezmaxes were steady at W90 and 80,000 tonne vessels (Aframaxes) at W105, while in the north 80,000 tonners were little changed at W90.
Fuel oil held firm with 25,000 tonne cargoes at W185 in the north and W190 in the Med.
"There's been some Baltic enquiry in UKC which is pushing rates up a bit. We haven't seen it in the Med yet, but maybe it's a question of time," one broker said.
In the Western Hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude rates were steady to slightly softer at W175, with 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes at W185.
